thought: A childhood tumor. Three spinal surgeries at 29. Paralyzed from the waist down. She took up competitive sport at 30 anyway.
support: Deepa Malik was diagnosed with a spinal tumor at age 5, requiring years of treatment and aggressive physiotherapy. The tumor recurred when she was 29; after three spinal surgeries, she was left paralyzed from the waist down. She began a competitive sports career at age 30 across shot put, javelin, discus, swimming and even motorcycle rallying. At the 2016 Rio Paralympics, at age 45, she won silver in shot put (F53 category) with a personal-best throw of 4.61m - becoming the first Indian woman to win a Paralympic medal. Over her career she has won 23 international medals and 58 national medals, and received the Padma Shri.
